questions.q: Which shortcut **centres** the selected paragraph in Word?
questions.solution: **Ctrl+E = cEntre.** Ctrl+C is copy; C was taken, so centre borrowed E.

questions.q: The Wi-Fi wireless LAN standard family is designated by IEEE:
questions.solution: IEEE 802.11 covers Wi-Fi (a/b/g/n/ac/ax). 802.3 is wired Ethernet, 802.15 Bluetooth/PAN, 802.16 WiMAX.

questions.q: Which statement is correct?
options: Ctrl+H shows history but Ctrl+H in Word opens Replace
Ctrl+H shows history in every program
Ctrl+D bookmarks a page and duplicates slides in Word
Alt+Home opens the browser's download page
questions.solution: Ctrl+H is **History in browsers, Replace in Word** — same keys, different apps. Ctrl+D duplicates slides in PowerPoint, not Word; the browser home page is Alt+Home (that part of option D is right but its download-page tail is wrong).
questions.shortcut: Same key, three apps, three jobs.

questions.q: A Class C network provides how many USABLE host addresses?
questions.solution: 256 total minus the **network address** and the **broadcast address** = **254 usable**.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: The true subject is **the number** (singular); *applicants* sits inside the 'of' phrase and cannot decide the verb. Part 2 must read **has doubled**. The other parts are grammatical.
questions.shortcut: Cover the 'of' phrase; the number is singular.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given phrase.

To look down upon
questions.solution: *Look down upon* = to think that someone is less important than oneself. 'Respect' is the opposite; 'from a height' is literal.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

We have run ___ of sugar; please buy some on your way home.
questions.solution: *Run out of* = to have no more left. Only *out* forms this phrase with *of*.

questions.q: Select the correct passive form of the sentence: 'Someone is auditing our accounts this week.'
options: Our accounts are been audited this week.
Our accounts are auditing this week.
Our accounts were being audited this week.
Our accounts are being audited this week.
questions.solution: Present continuous row with the vague *someone* dropped: **Our accounts are being audited this week.** 'Are been audited' misplaces been; 'are auditing' leaves the sentence active with the accounts doing the auditing; 'were being audited' shifts to the past row.
questions.shortcut: Continuous active → being + V3; drop the vague agent.

questions.q: The **Corruption Perceptions Index** is released by —
questions.solution: **Transparency International (Berlin)** publishes the CPI — higher score means a cleaner public sector.

questions.q: Under Article 243-I, a State Finance Commission is constituted once in how many years?
questions.solution: A **State Finance Commission every five years** (Art. 243-I) reviews the financial position of panchayats and municipalities, on the lines of the central Finance Commission (Art. 280).
questions.shortcut: FC (centre) and SFC (state) both run on 5-year cycles.

questions.q: A **transformer** works —
options: On both AC and DC equally
questions.solution: A transformer works by **mutual induction**, which needs a *changing* magnetic field — so it works only on alternating current. A steady DC gives no induced voltage.

questions.q: When **blue copper sulphate crystals** are heated strongly, they —
options: Turn white as water of crystallisation is lost
questions.solution: Heating drives off the 5H₂O; the anhydrous CuSO₄ left behind is **white** — and turns blue again if moistened.

questions.q: Ravi spends $\frac{1}{3}$ of his salary on rent and $\frac{1}{4}$ of the remaining on food. He saves the rest, which is ₹9,000. What is his salary?
questions.solution:
After rent, $\frac{2}{3}$ is left. Food $= \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{1}{6}$ of the salary.
Savings $= 1 - \frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$ of the salary $= ₹9,000$.
Salary $= ₹18,000$.
questions.shortcut: Trap ₹21,600: taking $\frac{1}{4}$ of the whole salary gives savings $\frac{5}{12}$.

questions.q: A train 180 m long crosses a 220 m long platform in 25 seconds. The speed of the train is:
What is 24% of 650?
A speed of 54 km/h expressed in m/s is:

Three of the following four pairs are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd pair.

**Hot : Cold, Up : Down, Rich : Poor, Big : Large**
questions.solution: Hot - cold, up - down and rich - poor are **opposites**. Big and large have the **same meaning** → **Big : Large**.

questions.q: If **a ▲ b = a − b** when a > b and **a ▲ b = a + b** when a ≤ b, find **(9 ▲ 4) ▲ 7**.
questions.solution: 9 ▲ 4: 9 > 4, so 9 − 4 = 5. Then 5 ▲ 7: 5 ≤ 7, so 5 + 7 = **12**. (−2 re-uses the first case without checking.)
questions.shortcut: Check the condition again at every step.

questions.q: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.solution: The inner square joins the midpoints; the diagonals of the outer square cross everything. Size by size: each corner triangle is split by a diagonal into 2 tiny ones → 8; the 4 corner triangles themselves → 4; the 4 triangles with a full side of the square as base and apex at the centre → 4; the 4 half-squares → 4. Total 8 + 4 + 4 + 4 = **20**.
questions.shortcut: Work outward: tiny, corner, centre-apex, half-square.

questions.q:
Three of the following four number-sets are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd set.
(**NOTE:** Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking them into their digits. For example, with 13 you may add, subtract or multiply 13 itself, but you may not split it into 1 and 3.)

**(7, 3, 20), (8, 5, 39), (6, 4, 23), (9, 2, 18)**
questions.shortcut: Third number is one less than the product in three sets, equal to it in one.
